spec_match.rationale: The fingerprinting analysis (AccentColor as a per-user bit readable via getComputedStyle, restricted outside installed-app scope) matches the change's rationale — but the page never performs the one-line read that would show the visitor their own engine's behavior.

interactive.rationale: Entirely static prose+table for a claim that is perfectly probeable: set color:AccentColor, read getComputedStyle, and report whether the engine resolved a system-specific colour, a fixed default, or (as measured here) doesn't support the keyword at all.

blurb_alignment.rationale: 'The attack' is described, never demonstrated — even though demonstrating it safely is trivial and instructive.

edge_cases.rationale: No handling of the three real states (supported+system colour / supported+masked / unsupported). Measured on Chromium 141 headless: CSS.supports('color','AccentColor') = false and the computed fallback is rgb(0,0,0) — a state the page doesn't even acknowledge exists.

references.rationale: Feature index links chromestatus; the before/after behavior table cites nothing.

conformance.rationale: Feature suite exists; page anchors nothing.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 CDP run + probe: AccentColor unsupported here (supports=false, computed rgb(0,0,0)); rendering clean — 0px overflow both classes, zero console errors.

openQuestions.title: Perform the read this page is about
openQuestions.detail: Add a live panel: swatch styled color:AccentColor, its getComputedStyle value, CSS.supports check, and display-mode context — reporting which of the three states the visitor's engine is in (system colour exposed / masked per this change / keyword unsupported, the measured state here). The 'attack' becomes a safe, honest one-liner demo.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Demonstrate fingerprinting surfaces with transparent, local-only reads.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: NOT applied — filed as the major question; this critique's probe supplied the first measurement.

summary: Reviewed headlessly (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): a fingerprinting explainer that never performs its own one-line probe — which this review did, finding the keyword entirely unsupported on the test engine (a third state the page doesn't mention). Major live-panel question filed.
